events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
Dispute type is safety, filed by the rider, alleging that the driver sped, braked hard and overtook on the shoulder for the whole trip [F1][F2][F3][F4]. Under SAFE-2, a case involving a dangerous-driving allegation is not decided on the papers but escalated to a human reviewer, with the summary noting the 995 / driver's commercial insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths [SAFE-2][F2]. This is the mandatory path regardless of how thin the corroboration is, so no substantive finding for or against either party is made here.

The threat trigger of SAFE-1 is not met: the two in-app messages are purely logistical (rider's location at the main entrance, driver's arrival notice) and contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or abuse, so SAFE-1 does not apply and escalation rests on SAFE-2 alone [F3][F4][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Both advocates correctly concede this point (C2, D3, rebuttal C2).

What happened: the rider was matched for a RydeX trip Jurong East MRT → NUS, pickup 21:22, drop-off 21:34, for a fixed quote of $21.04. The rider claims she felt scared and unsafe because of the driver's speed, hard braking and shoulder overtaking; the driver denies it, stating he drove normally and the rider was on the phone the whole trip and never complained [F5]. What is disputed is therefore the manner of driving — instantaneous speed, acceleration, braking and lane position — which the file contains no telematics fact to measure. The ambient records are neutral rather than decisive: actual distance 8.5 km versus 8.6 km optimal (−0.1 km, −1%, no off-route segment) and duration 12.8 min versus a 14 min estimate (−1.0 min) [F1][F2]. Neither the length of the path nor the end-to-end duration establishes or refutes lawful speed, braking or lane use, so I do not treat them as corroboration either way [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

Facts a human reviewer should check: whether any telematics/vehicle data or LTA DataMall incident or speed-band record exists for the corridor in the 21:22–21:34 window [F1][F2]; why no report was raised in-app at the time, given the chat shows no complaint or expression of fear and the rider's only written report is the dispute narrative [F3][F4][F5]; and whether the driver's statement that the rider was on the phone is verifiable or merely self-serving [F5]. Profile facts (rider: 3.6 y, 4.5 rating, 0 disputes in 90 d; driver: 3.5 y, 4.82 rating, 345 trips in 90 d, 0 disputes/0 upheld) are context only and cannot decide the safety question, and since no breach is established, no account flag is warranted [F6][F7][RD-6][SAFE-2].

No monetary remedy is available or appropriate: the RydeX fare is a fixed quote unaffected by mileage, no off-route segment exists, and no supplemental charge (ERP/toll, waiting fee, destination-change fee, cancellation fee) is in dispute, so FARE-1 generates no refund item and the amount is null [F1][F2][FARE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human review as a safety/dangerous-driving report: preserve the trip telematics and chat log, obtain the rider's and driver's accounts, and inform the rider of the 995 / driver commercial insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths. No fare adjustment is to be made in the meantime.

certificate: ✗ SAFE-1 threat / intimidation language present [case] threat keyword table (core/facts/tools.py) (no evidence)

claims.assertion: The rider reported a safety incident — the driver allegedly speeding, braking hard and overtaking on the shoulder throughout the trip — which is a dangerous-driving allegation on the face of the complaint.

No chat message contains any threat, intimidation, harassment or abuse by either party; the two messages are purely logistical (rider's location, driver's ETA), so SAFE-1's threat trigger is not met and the escalation basis is SAFE-2 only.

The GPS record shows actual distance 8.5 km versus an optimal 8.6 km (−0.1 km, −1%), so there is no evidence of a longer or evasive route that could corroborate the driving-conduct complaint either way.

Actual trip duration was 12.8 min against a 14 min estimate (−1.0 min), i.e. the trip was completed no slower than estimated; this is consistent with the trip being completed normally and does not itself corroborate the speeding allegation.

The driver's only denial is his written statement that he 'drove normally', which is a statement that does not displace gps/timeline records under the system-record-wins rule and cannot resolve the disputed driving conduct.

The driver has 345 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld in that window, and the rider has 0 disputes in 90 days; neither profile supports a flag_account request or a finding of repeated misconduct.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is documented only in the dispute narrative; the chat record contains no report of unsafe driving at the time, and the driver's statement (F5) says the rider never complained, so there is no contemporaneous rider-side evidence of the alleged speeding, hard braking or shoulder overtaking.

The available system records point mildly the other way: distance −0.1 km vs optimal (F1) and duration −1.0 min vs estimate (F2) show a normal, non-diverted, on-time trip, which the driver can use (with F5) to argue the ride was unremarkable.

The driver's clean record (F7: 4.82 rating, 345 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days) will be used by the other side to argue the safety allegation is out of character, and my own profile evidence (F6/F7) does not support any account flag.

No fare facts exist for this case, so I cannot request any monetary remedy such as a refund or fee waiver; the only viable route to relief is escalation for human review, and the policy does not provide a rider-side compensation for a dangerous-driving allegation.
No traffic or weather facts are available (get_traffic_facts returned none), so no objective road-condition corroboration of the driving style can be produced on my side.

claims.assertion: The rider's speeding allegation is not corroborated by any system record: the completed trip took 12.8 min against a 14 min estimate (F2), and no speed-related or hazard evidence exists in the case file for this trip.

The rider's claim of unsafe overtaking / hard braking on the shoulder is contradicted by the route record showing the driver's path was shorter than optimal (8.5 km actual vs 8.6 km optimal, -0.1 km) with no off-route segment, i.e. no excursion consistent with shoulder use or erratic routing (F1).

The only contemporaneous in-app messages are logistics only — rider at the main entrance in a blue shirt (F3) and the driver's arrival notice in a white Honda Vezel (F4) — with no complaint, safety concern or threat raised by either side during or at the end of the trip.

The driver's account that he drove normally and the rider never raised any complaint (F5) is consistent with the trip record (F1, F2) and with the absence of any message of concern in the chat (F3, F4), so nothing in the file supports an unsafe-driving finding.

There is no traffic, weather or incident fact in this case file, and no accident, injury or dangerous-driving record exists, so the rider's safety complaint rests on her unaided recollection and does not satisfy the escalation threshold of a documented incident (F1, F2, F6).

The driver's record supports no adverse action: 3.5 years on the platform, 4.82 rating, 345 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints (F7), which is inconsistent with the profile of a dangerous driver.

The rider pays a fixed RydeX quote of $21.04 and the trip was completed as quoted (F1, F2); no element of the fare was generated by an unsafe or deviating route, so no refund or fee waiver is owed to her on this record.

weaknesses: The dispute type is a safety allegation and there is no GPS or telematics fact that measures instantaneous speed, acceleration, braking or lane position, so the driver cannot positively prove normal driving — the case rests on the absence of corroboration rather than on exculpatory data (F1, F2).

The rider's complaint is detailed and specific ('speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder'), and although the ride was shorter than the estimate (F2), the 12.8 min duration over 8.5 km is consistent with a brisk pace and could be read by a human reviewer as some support for her account (F1, F2).

The driver's own statement is interested testimony and the fact that the rider was on the phone 'the whole trip' (F5) does not explain why no report was raised at drop-off, so a reviewer may weigh F5 as self-serving rather than as corroboration.

Under SAFE-2, a safety allegation involving dangerous driving is normally escalated to human review rather than decided on the papers, so the driver cannot obtain a clean no_action without an escalation step; the rider's clean 90-day history and 4.5 rating (F6) may also be used by the other side to argue the complaint is credible.

points.response: Concede the arithmetic but not the conclusion: F2 (12.8 min vs 14 min estimate) shows only end-to-end duration, and no clause makes an on-time arrival evidence of lawful speed, acceleration or braking behaviour during the trip.

F1 measures route length (8.5 km vs 8.6 km optimal) and has no bearing on lane position, so a −0.1 km path cannot contradict an allegation of shoulder overtaking; the driver's admitted weakness concedes no telematics fact measures speed, acceleration, braking or lane position.

Conceded as to the content of the chat: F3 and F4 are logistics only, and I do not assert any message of complaint; the absence of an in-app message is not an element of SAFE-2, which triggers on the dangerous-driving allegation in the case.

F5 is the driver's own interested statement and, under the system-record-wins rule, a statement alone cannot resolve a factual contest about driving conduct; it is not corroboration for the driver's position it asserts.

The driver's own admitted weakness already concedes that a dangerous-driving allegation is normally escalated rather than decided on the papers (F1, F2), and SAFE-2 does not require a documented incident, injury or record as a precondition; the rider's clean 90-day history (F6) removes any suggestion of a vexatious filer.

F7 is a profile fact, admissible only in support of an outcome or a flag_account request and never to decide the case alone, so 345 dispute-free trips and a 4.82 rating cannot dispose of the safety allegation — and I request no flag against the driver.
Not contested: I claim no refund, and FARE-1 governs unpublished or unsupported add-ons, not safety; my requested outcome was and remains escalate with no amount.

My claim C1 asserts only what the complaint alleges and that SAFE-2 routes dangerous-driving allegations to human review; it makes no finding of fact against the driver, which is precisely why escalation rather than adjudication is the correct action.
Clarifying rather than withdrawing: F2 shows the trip was no slower than the 14 min estimate, which is neutral as between the parties, and I do not rely on it to prove unsafe speed.

A bare allegation of dangerous driving on the face of a complaint is not itself evidence; the system records show a normal 8.5 km trip in 12.8 min against a 14 min estimate (F1, F2), so escalating on the rider's narrative alone would put a clean record on the line with no corroboration.

Conceded — the two chat messages are purely logistical (rider's location, driver's arrival notice) and contain no threat, so SAFE-1 is not triggered; that agreement also means there is no contemporaneous message of fear or complaint from the rider while the alleged conduct was happening.

Accepted, and it cuts against the rider: the driver's path was 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route (F1) with no off-route segment, which is inconsistent with the swerving, shoulder-overtaking conduct alleged and also shows no fare-generating deviation.

The rider's own advocate concedes the duration record does not corroborate the speeding allegation; I go further — 12.8 min over 8.5 km is an ordinary urban pace and no fact in this file records any speed excess (F1, F2).

My client's statement (F5) is not offered to displace the system records — it is offered because it is consistent with them: the ride was unremarkable in distance and time (F1, F2) and the rider sent no message of fear during or after the trip (F3, F4).

Both advocates agree on the profile facts: the rider has 0 disputes in 90 days and my client has 345 trips in 90 days with a 4.82 rating and 0 disputes or upheld complaints (F6, F7), so no flag_account is warranted and there is no pattern of misconduct supporting relief.

I narrow D5 for precision: the file contains no traffic, weather or incident fact at all for this trip, so there is no objective road-condition or incident evidence on either side and neither party can build a finding on an empty record (F1, F2, F6).
